title: How Does ADA Staking Work?
description:
From the outside, Cardano Staking can look like a pyramid scheme leading you to ask the question how does ADA staking actually work?  In this video we break down in simple terms how and why you receive ADA rewards.

Join our Telegram group - https://t.me/+3o2Nv1qkFmYwNDg8

Stake your ADA using the ticker UPSTR

Upstream is an ADA staking pool dedicated to providing the Cardano community with a reliable and lovingly maintained node 24/7. Simple, accessible financial education is at the heart of our decisions, helping you to join our journey to become financially independent Upstreamers!

Join us to help support financial charities.

Website - https://upstream.org.uk/
Twitter - https://twitter.com/Upstream_ada
Facebook - https://www.facebook.com/UpstreamStaking

0:00 What is this video about?
0:25 Is ADA staking a pyramid scheme?
0:40 How does the Cardano network run?
1:09 Where do the rewards come from?
1:33 How are the rewards split?
1:57 How are stake pools chosen to produce a block?
2:44 How do I choose a stake pool?
3:34 Big or small?
3:55 Next steps

asr.full_text: Welcome back upstreamers, I'm Dave and today we're talking about ADA staking. How does it work, why do you get rewards and how do you picking which staking pool to delegate your ADA to and no i'm not only going to give you the easy answer of upstairing. This isn't an in depth look at the technicalities of the staking mechanism. You'll know that I'm the most intelligent one in the upstream team but that's not what this video is about. Instead, you should see this more of a beginner's guide to staking. looking from the outside staking rewards can look like a pyramid scheme... you know those scams at work by getting more people into the ecosystem on the bottom to pay off early adopters at the top but Cardano staking couldn't be further from that. to understand staking rewards you need to have a basic understanding of how the Cardano network runs. Basically, there are over 3000 nodes or small computers around the world which have the chance to confirm transactions on Cardano blockchain in 22nd slots. Going forward, we're going to use the words node and pool. The node is the little computer that runs the network. And the pool, or st staking pool is where people delegate their ADA to support the node more on that later. All the transactions made on the network during this time are patched together and become a block. Oh hey, blockchain. Makes sense now. Each transaction has a small fee attached to it. The majority of the fees for processing these transactions are then given out to the people who have delegated their ADA to the pool. This happens only after a set fee is taken out for the person who runs the node which goes towards their running costs. The bigger the proportion of the ADA in the pool that is yours the bigger the share of the rewards you will get. So lets talk some real numbers so you can see how this actually breaks down so let's say the pool has one million ADA delegated to it in total and you have 100 000 ADA in there this means that you would receive 10 percent of the pool rewards but with over 3 000 staking pools to choose from how do you know where to put your ADA? To help make this decision, it is good to know which pool is chosen to produce a block. You can think of each ADA token in a staking pool as a raffle ticket, this raffle ticket is to win the chance to produce a block. The more ADA there is in a staking pool, the more raffle tickets they will have. Simply put, the more ADA in a pool, the more chance of producing a block. This is how Cardano bills trust with the nodes on the network the more ADA in the staking pool the more trust that, that node is well maintained and is capable of running the network. If it wasn't then the node wouldn't be producing blocks the delegators wouldn't be getting their rewards and they have moved their ADA to another pool meaning that staking pool has less of a chance of producing a block so you might think that delegating to a pool with more AIDA in it would give you more rewards as that pool is more likely to produce more blocks but it's not quite as simple as that remember when I said that you get a proportion of the rewards relative to how much aid are you having the pool well if you Delegate to a pool with a smaller amount of total delegated ADA, they will produce less blocks over time, but you'll get a higher proportion of the rewards. Whereas, if you delegate you ADA to a pool with more total ADA, they will produce more blocks, but you will get a smaller proportion of rewards. This all sounds very complicated, but, to make things easier, if you stake to a pool that is actively producing blocks Then you should average three to four point five percent Api or three to four point five percent in Ada rewards across the year in our view It's good to support the smaller pools who don't produce many blocks as this helps stop big players with lots of money from setting up lots of staking pools and basically owning the network. If you are feeling really generous, then you could support pools that haven't produced any blocks yet at all. But maybe the best idea is to have a few accounts using an eternal wallet and spread your ADA across a few different pools. If you wanna know how to set up an eternal wallet on mobile, you can check out this little video up here. Wanna see more helpful card on our content? Then makes sure you slap that subscribe button and help us out by giving this video a little like. It really does make a difference. Until next time, grab your paddle and head upstream. Thank You For Watching!

textual.context: The description presents the video as financial education and the ASR explains how Cardano staking rewards are distributed. The description also promotes the Upstream staking pool and provides external contact and website links; whether the return statement is a guarantee is unclear.
textual.potential_relevance: The claimed ADA return is directly connected to the requested action of delegating ADA to a named staking pool, requiring later assessment of the offer's terms and presentation.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish that any return is guaranteed, that funds were transferred, that the pool operates as described, or that the external destinations, identity, or outcomes were verified.

textual_context_notes.observation: The source explicitly discusses and rejects the comparison between Cardano staking rewards and a pyramid scheme.

evidence.quote: looking from the outside staking rewards can look like a pyramid scheme
but Cardano staking couldn't be further from that

annotation.contextual_rationale: The video combines a beginner staking guide with a direct invitation to stake ADA using the UPSTR ticker, linking the requested financial participation to a stated average annual reward of 3% to 4.5% in ADA for actively producing pools. Although the speaker explains how rewards are distributed and rejects the pyramid-scheme comparison, the supplied records do not establish that the quoted range is guaranteed, that any viewer transferred ADA, or what outcome followed.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary mechanism is participation in ADA staking through delegation to a pool, with rewards described as coming from transaction fees and linked to the amount of ADA delegated. The video also states an expected average annual ADA reward range for an actively producing pool.
